title: Window: Agent Approval Laundering — transitive effects beyond approved invocation (arXiv 2609.28586, Sep 23)
claim: Defines approval laundering: durable approval records name entry invocations but omit transitive workflow effects (npm lifecycle, MCP network, etc.). Across 111 pairs residuals fall 40→13 with metadata; effect-bound records cut residuals 10→3. Claude Code PreToolUse PoC. Complements SEP-2640 / coding-agent permission gates.
excerpt: We call the resulting structural record-coverage failure approval laundering: a durable record faithfully names the entry invocation yet omits effects exercised within its workflow.

title: Window: Progressive Skill Discovery as access control for tool-using agents (arXiv 2609.28693, Sep 23)
claim: Argues exposing full enterprise toolsets via prompts is unsafe; proposes progressive skill discovery as structural governance — role-scoped capability delivery so policies become hard constraints rather than probabilistic advice. Intersects IntentCap / Stochastic Deputy HOLDs.
excerpt: Providing an agent with access to every internal tool leads to oversized context windows, degraded tool selection, and severe governance vulnerabilities — as system policies defined purely in prompts remain probabilistic advice rather than hard constraints.

title: Window: Evaluating Agent Skills for version-specific plugin migration (arXiv 2609.30120, Sep 24)

excerpt: Agent skills package version-specific maintenance knowledge for coding agents, but a higher diagnostic score does not by itself show that the resulting migration advice satisfies the target version's contract.
